planId: 1.1.5-rc.4 v1 (draft until the product owner approves)
purpose: First full run under the release test procedure: suite A (every case) on every machine, suite B (confirmation of each fix in rc.4), suites C and D (acceptance of new features, install and update).
selectNote: Cases come from the case catalog (release-checks/cases). An empty select runs every automated case for this platform; chosen cases that are not automated are listed in the report as not covered. Smoke cases (suite smoke) are the most used paths.
caseTimeoutNote: 15 min: N1 (a new user) downloads and installs the runtime inside the case.
confirmationNote: Suite cases that confirm a fix in rc.4. Keep only those whose fix is in rc.4; add the case of every other fix before the plan is frozen.

acceptance.title: Confirmation of the fix: Removing the chosen image provider silently turns off image generation while Settings > Tools still shows Shisa.AI
steps: Do the steps under 'What happens' in the issue filed for this finding, on this build
Sign in to Shisa.AI and to ChatGPT.
In Settings > Tools, choose ChatGPT (gpt-image-2) as the image provider.
Remove ChatGPT from Model providers.
expected: One rule decides which image provider is in effect, and the Tools card and the extension both use it. When the saved provider is removed, the choice falls back to a usable provider that the card shows and lets the user change, or the card says plainly that no provider is available. Image generation is never off while the card shows it as on.
acceptance.evidence: screenshot of the end state and of each step that the issue shows

acceptance.title: Confirmation of the fix: The Shisa.AI sign-in failure message covers the button to try again
steps: Do the steps under 'What happens' in the issue filed for this finding, on this build
expected: The failure message never covers the action that recovers from it. It sits beside the button, or the button stays reachable.
acceptance.evidence: screenshot of the end state and of each step that the issue shows

acceptance.title: Confirmation of the fix: After a reload, an old sign-in failure is shown as if it had just happened
steps: Do the steps under 'What happens' in the issue filed for this finding, on this build
expected: A failure message belongs to the attempt that produced it. After a reload the provider shows its current state (signed in or not), and an earlier failure is either gone or clearly marked with when it happened.
acceptance.evidence: screenshot of the end state and of each step that the issue shows

acceptance.title: Confirmation of the fix: Signing in to ChatGPT changes the New session default model
steps: Do the steps under 'What happens' in the issue filed for this finding, on this build
expected: Adding a provider makes its models available. It never changes the user's chosen default model. The default changes only when the user picks another one, or when the chosen model is no longer available. In that case the UI says so.
acceptance.evidence: screenshot of the end state and of each step that the issue shows

acceptance.title: Confirmation of the fix: The same provider is shown under three different names, and an OAuth sign-in is shown as "Key saved"
steps: Do the steps under 'What happens' in the issue filed for this finding, on this build
expected: One display name per provider, used everywhere. The provider's state describes how it is connected (signed in vs key saved).
acceptance.evidence: screenshot of the end state and of each step that the issue shows

acceptance.title: Confirmation of the fix: At a window width of 800 px the review card overflows and its Deny button is cut off

acceptance.title: Confirmation of the fix: When the image extension is not loaded, the host's image refresh command is sent to the model as a user message

expected: The host sends the refresh only to a runtime where the extension is loaded (for example, it checks the runtime's command list first). A missing extension shows up as a clear image tool state, never as a model turn.

acceptance.title: First run of the DMG app installs the runtime on its own
steps: Copy the .app from the DMG to R/pkg and clear its quarantine attribute
Start it with a throwaway home: HOME=R/home-fresh, run the app's MacOS binary
Wait on the start page until it is ready
Open a new session and send one message with any model the fresh home offers
expected: The start page shows install steps with progress
No 'runtime missing' message and no Retry button
The start page reaches ready
Runtime files are created only under R/home-fresh
acceptance.evidence: screenshots of install progress and ready state; a listing of R/home-fresh

acceptance.title: Quitting or killing the app leaves no host or runtime
steps: With the app from D-mac-1 running, press Cmd+Q
List processes whose command line contains R
Start it again, then kill -9 the app process
After 5 s list processes again
expected: After Cmd+Q no jouzu-host or runtime process from R is running
5 s after kill -9 no jouzu-host or runtime process from R is running
acceptance.evidence: the two process listings

acceptance.title: Runtime files deleted while the app runs are reinstalled
steps: With the app running on R/home-fresh, delete the runtime's files under that home
Watch the start page / status for up to 60 s
Open a session and send one message
expected: The app shows that it is reinstalling the runtime
The runtime is back within 60 s
The session replies
acceptance.evidence: screenshots during and after reinstall

acceptance.title: #239 A folder opened through a symlink is listed once

acceptance.title: Image tool with a free Shisa.AI account
steps: In the throwaway home, sign in with the free Shisa.AI account (the product owner signs in when asked)
Open Settings > Tools
In a chat, ask for an image
expected: Settings > Tools shows Shisa.AI as the provider and says the plan has no image generation
The chat answer gives that reason
Chat keeps working after it
acceptance.evidence: screenshots of Settings > Tools and the chat

acceptance.title: Model list follows sign-in without a restart
steps: Note the New session model list
Sign in
Open the New session model list
Sign out
Open the list again
expected: After sign-in the list has the account's models without a restart
After sign-out those models are gone
acceptance.evidence: screenshots of the three lists

acceptance.title: In-place update 1.1.4 -> rc.4 keeps data and sign-ins
steps: As the machine's normal test user (the Windows upgrade machine is a test machine; no second user): move the app's real data and install folders aside so the item starts clean
Install 1.1.4 and use it (sessions, a sign-in, a setting changed)
Update through the QA channel to rc.4
Open the app
Restore the folders moved aside at the start
expected: All sessions are listed and open
Sign-ins are kept
Changed settings are kept
What's new shows the rc.4 notes as paragraphs and list items
acceptance.evidence: screenshots before and after

acceptance.title: In-place update rc.2 -> rc.4 keeps data, sign-ins and the runtime
steps: As the machine's normal test user (the Windows upgrade machine is a test machine; no second user): move the app's real data and install folders aside so the item starts clean
With rc.2 installed and used, update through the QA channel to rc.4
Open the app
Look at the runtime version and install log
Restore the folders moved aside at the start
expected: All sessions, sign-ins and settings are kept
Runtime 0.2.5 is kept, not downloaded again
A session running when the update started was stopped first; the window does not stay on 'Preparing Jouzu'
acceptance.evidence: screenshots; the host log lines about the runtime

acceptance.title: Install folder after the update
steps: As the machine's normal test user (the Windows upgrade machine is a test machine; no second user): move the app's real data and install folders aside so the item starts clean
After D-upg-1 or D-upg-2, list the install folder
Open Settings > System
Restore the folders moved aside at the start
expected: No files left from the old version (for example an old icon)
Jouzu's Git Bash is present and in use
The commit shown has no 'dirty'
acceptance.evidence: folder listing; screenshot of Settings > System

acceptance.title: Image tool with a paid Shisa.AI account and with ChatGPT
steps: Start the unpacked rc.4 host and UI on a throwaway home
Sign in to Shisa.AI (paid) and ChatGPT in that home
Open Settings > Tools
Ask for an image in en and in ja
Choose the other provider and ask again
Turn the tool off and ask again in the next turn
Remove the chosen provider and open Settings > Tools
expected: Settings > Tools shows the provider in use
An image is generated
With both signed in the provider can be chosen
With the tool off it is not offered in the next turn
After removing the chosen provider, Settings > Tools shows the provider now in effect, or that none is
acceptance.evidence: screenshots of each step

acceptance.title: AppImage and .deb first run, quit and kill
steps: Run the AppImage with a throwaway home
Install the .deb with apt in a clean container and start it with a throwaway home
Close the window; then start again and kill -9 the app
Delete the runtime files while the app runs
expected: Both reach ready with install progress shown, no 'missing' and no Retry
After closing and 5 s after kill -9 no host or runtime is left
The runtime is reinstalled within 60 s and a session replies
acceptance.evidence: screenshots; process listings; host log lines

severity.S1: data loss, app crash or unusable, security, wasting the user's money (for example tokens spent)
severity.S2: core function broken with no workaround (send, sessions, sign-in, image tool silently off)
severity.S3: broken with a workaround, or the UI shows a wrong state

runAs: a normal user account (not root, not an administrator) on every machine; the runner refuses to start otherwise
